sections.h2: Selling in a growing town like Ennis
sections.html:
Ennis has grown quickly and carries higher home values, so sellers here compete with new construction. The city had 25,694 residents in July 2025, a 27.6% jump from an April 2020 base of 20,133.

A fast-growing town gives an older house two kinds of buyers: families who prefer an established lot and investors who see rental demand. A direct sale suits someone who cannot wait for either. Think about how your house stacks up against new homes nearby before you pick an asking price.

  • Direct buyer: house taken as is, date agreed together.
  • Agent listing: the broadest audience, with showings.
  • Family sale: quick on price, still needs a recorded deed.

These figures show what homes and households look like in town, which helps you read an offer.

Ennis housing and household figures, 2020-2024 estimates

A 27.6 minute average trip suggests many residents work outside town, so a listing that explains road access to larger job centers can help. Keep the description to facts you can check.

Buyers lean toward households with children and steady jobs. Children are 25.7% of residents and seniors 12.7%. Median household income is $75,074, and per capita income is $33,059.

Owner costs run $1,991 a month with a mortgage and $670 without, so a buyer financing a home needs an income near the local median to carry a typical payment. About 89.2% of residents lived at the same address a year before, so streets feel settled. A third, 33.8%, use another language at home, so a bilingual listing is useful.

  • Families: yards, schools and a quiet street.
  • Commuters: road access toward larger job centers.
  • Investors: a rent near $1,362 weighed against price.

sections.h2: What permits the City of Ennis requires
sections.html:
The city requires a permit before anyone builds, alters, enlarges, moves, demolishes or repairs a structure inside city limits. Buyers ask for those records, so gather them early.

  • Accessory buildings over 120 square feet.
  • Demolition and moving a structure.
  • Drive approaches and irrigation systems.
  • Fences taller than 8 feet.
  • Signs, swimming pools and spas.

Planning and Development is at 108 W. Knox Street, (972) 875-6442, open weekdays from eight to five. Its page links a Historic District information page, a zoning verification letter and a tool to find your zoning district. Use them to answer a buyer who wants to add a shed or a pool.

sections.h2: Lot size and what shoppers notice
sections.html:
Ennis covers 32.50 land square miles, up from 27.65 in 2010, with 620.2 residents per square mile in 2020. That leaves more room per resident than in a dense city, so lot size and yard space are real selling points.

Most buyers begin online, so show clear photos, an accurate floor plan and the age of the roof and cooling system.

  • Lot size: mention it, since density is low.
  • Photos: shoot in daylight and include the back yard.
  • Records: list recent roof, plumbing or cooling work.

sections.h2: How long a buyer waits on an Ennis permit
sections.html:
The city prints plan review times by project size, which helps a buyer who plans renovations after closing.

  • Small residential projects and minor additions: 1 to 3 days.
  • New residential construction and major additions: 3 to 10 days.
  • Small commercial projects and minor additions: 3 to 10 days.
  • New commercial construction and major additions: 14 to 28 days.

Workload can change these times. The permit holder schedules inspections, and the city has an online portal for permits and inspections. If your buyer wants to add a room, quote these ranges so the buyer can plan the timeline.

sections.h2: Tax bills at an Ennis closing
sections.html:
The appraisal district sets value, local units set rates, and a lien for the year attaches January 1. A sale later in the year divides the bill at the closing table.

Homesteads receive a school exemption, owners 65 or older or disabled get added relief, and a homestead's appraised value is capped at 10% growth a year. Bills reach owners in autumn and may be paid in two halves.

  • Ask the county tax office for your balance.
  • Request a tax certificate for closing.
  • Protest a value in spring if it looks wrong.

Pull together the records a title company asks for, and present the house the way a buyer comparing it with new construction would want to see it.

  • Deed, loan payoff letter and latest tax bill.
  • Permit and inspection records for pools, fences, sheds and drive approaches.
  • The zoning district for your lot from the city's lookup tool.
  • Receipts for roof, cooling and plumbing work.

A median gross rent of $1,362 makes Ennis appealing to landlords, so mention whether the house suits a tenant. If your street sits in a historic area, ask the planning office about exterior rules before you promise anything to a buyer. Clean, bright rooms and a tidy yard matter when buyers can compare your house against new builds on the edge of town.

Walk the lot with the zoning lookup open and note any setbacks or easements the buyer should know about. If you plan to leave appliances, list them in the contract so nothing is disputed at the final walk-through. Ask your title company to check for open permits or liens a few days before listing, which gives you time to fix surprises without pressure from a contract deadline.

A sale before an auction is allowed, and the lender is paid from the proceeds. After a default notice you have a short window to catch up, and a sale notice must precede the monthly auction by weeks.

The county clerk files the deed after notary acknowledgment and charges by the page. For an inherited house, several routes exist for smaller estates, and your title company will say which proof it needs.

Start with the payoff letter and the tax balance, since those two numbers decide what you net. Next ask the city planning office about permits for any past work, and check the zoning district if a buyer mentions a pool, a shed or a rental. Then compare offers on the same terms: the price, the date, who pays title costs, and whether the house must be empty at closing.

Cash buyers may skip an appraisal and a loan approval, which can shorten the calendar. Financed buyers bring a lender's timetable and sometimes repair requests. In a town where new homes compete for the same shoppers, a clear folder of records and a firm closing date make your house the easier choice. Keep a copy of every document you send, with the date, so nothing is lost if a buyer changes agents or lenders.

faqs.q: How fast can an Ennis sale close?
faqs.a: The buyer and the title company set the date. Ask for it in writing and keep your payoff letter ready.

faqs.q: Does Ennis require a permit for an old addition?
faqs.a: Ask Planning and Development at (972) 875-6442. The city requires a permit for work that alters or enlarges a structure.

faqs.q: Does Ennis have a historic district?
faqs.a: The city website lists a Historic District information page and a Historic Landmark Commission. Ask whether your address is covered.

faqs.q: Who sets property tax for an Ennis home?
faqs.a: Local units set rates and the appraisal district sets value. Ask the county tax office for your balance.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ennis house with a mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan is paid from the proceeds at closing, so request a payoff statement from your lender.
